title: Germany: AfD wins in northeastern state, Left in Berlin
summary: The far-right AfD has come first in the state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, with Chancellor Merz's CDU failing to enter parliament. Meanwhile the Left Party took first place in Berlin.…
byline: Darko Janjevic, Richard Connor, Kieran Burke, Roshni Majumdar

image.caption: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the two state election outcomes 'a disaster'Image: Christian Mang/REUTERS

blocks.text: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) scored another election victory on Sunday evening, becoming the strongest party in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania with 37.9% of the vote, according to an exit poll by the polling firm infratest-dimap on election night.

Even before the first exit poll results were announced, AfD co-leader Tino Churpalla told public TV network ARD, "We clearly have a mandate to govern here," before adding that the party would offer coalition talks to all the other parties.
Chrupalla also said he expected Chancellor Friedrich Merz to resign now. "That would truly be a relief for this country," he said.
